Log-linear daily interpolation of grab samples, with a span cap

Source: R/interpolate_loglinear.R
interpolate_loglinear.Rd

Fills a grid of days from a point's own grab samples ("anchors"). Between two anchors the value is interpolated linearly in log(value) (so the midpoint of a span is the geometric mean of its ends), or linearly in value when log = FALSE. This is the toxicant interpolation used by mspaf_pipeline() with ara_form = "added_hazard".

Usage

interpolate_loglinear(
  dates,
  values,
  detected,
  grid,
  span_cap = 120,
  log = TRUE
)

Arguments

dates

Date vector of anchor (sample) dates. Must be unique; any order.

values

Numeric anchor values, one per date.

detected

Logical, one per date. FALSE marks a below-detection anchor; NA is treated as TRUE.

grid

Date vector of the days to fill, in any order.

span_cap

Maximum anchor-to-anchor span (and hold after the last anchor) in days. Default 120. Inf disables the cap.

log

Logical. Interpolate in log(value) (default) or in value. With log = TRUE anchors with an NA or non-positive value are dropped; with log = FALSE only NA anchors are dropped.

Value

A data frame with one row per element of grid, in grid order, and columns date (= grid), value (numeric) and detected (logical). With no usable anchor every row is NA.

Span cap

A day is only filled when the anchors that bracket it are close enough together. For a grid day g, with x_i the last anchor on or before g:

  • there is no anchor on or before g: the day is uncovered (leading days are never back-filled);

  • g is an anchor date: the anchor's own value and detection flag;

  • g is after the last anchor: covered only while g - x_last <= span_cap, holding the last anchor's value and flag;

  • otherwise, with x_j the next anchor: covered only when x_j - x_i <= span_cap, and then interpolated between the two anchors.

Uncovered days have value = NA and detected = NA. span_cap = Inf disables the cap, so every day after the first anchor is covered.

Below-detection anchors

A below-detection anchor (detected = FALSE) enters the interpolation at the value supplied for it (the caller decides: the detection limit, half of it, ...). An interpolated day is flagged detected = FALSE only when both bracketing anchors are below detection; one detected anchor is enough to make the day detected. An anchor date, or a held day after the last anchor, carries that anchor's own flag.

See also

mspaf_pipeline() (ara_form = "added_hazard")

Examples

d0 <- as.Date("2024-01-01")
interpolate_loglinear(
  dates = d0 + c(0, 10, 200), values = c(2, 8, 4),
  detected = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE), grid = d0 + c(-1, 0, 5, 10, 100, 330)
)
#>         date value detected
#> 1 2023-12-31    NA       NA
#> 2 2024-01-01     2     TRUE
#> 3 2024-01-06     4     TRUE
#> 4 2024-01-11     8    FALSE
#> 5 2024-04-10    NA       NA
#> 6 2024-11-26    NA       NA
